title: Adaptive microburst-aware SLI calibration + chaos simulation for multi-region failover and circuit hysteresis
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Add a microburst-aware instrumentation and calibration pipeline for token-level latency SLIs, wire up a chaos-sim harness that simulates multi-region microbursts and controlled capacity loss, and iterate on circuit-breaker hysteresis and load-shed thresholds using closed-loop experiments. This ticket covers metric schema changes, dashboard panels, synthetic traffic scenarios, and an automated calibration job that recommends adjustments to per-route circuit parameters based on observed microburst frequency and KV-cache hit behavior.

Background: We continue to see short-duration (1–10s) spikes in token-level tail latency tied to traffic microbursts from a subset of customers. Existing SLI windows and static circuit thresholds either: 1) overreact and shed traffic for benign bursts, or 2) under-react and allow tail latency to breach SLOs during prolonged overload. We need instrumentation that captures microburst characteristics, a simulator to validate policies across regions, and dashboards + alerts that reflect microburst-aware SLIs.

Key deliverables:
- New metrics and tags for microburst detection and attribution (see Metrics Changes).
- Synthetic microburst traffic harness (k6 + short-burst generator) that can run as a scheduled Canary across regions to validate failover and shedding policies. Canary should run hourly and produce a report.
- Dashboards: microburst timeline, per-route circuit state heatmap, KV-cache hit correlation, and canary run summary panel.
- Calibration job: batch job that analyzes the last 72h of microburst events and recommends circuit hysteresis parameters (open threshold, cooldown, backoff multiplier) per route and per-region.
- Runbook snippets for operators describing how to interpret microburst indicators and when to adjust autoscaling vs shed parameters.

Non-goals: full rollout of auto-tuning; that will be a follow-up after we validate calibration signals and safety checks.
acceptance_criteria: New metric names emitted to telemetry ingestion for microburst detection: request.token_latency_ms (with token_index tag), request.microburst_flag (0|1), request.microburst_window_ms, request.microburst_count_in_1m
Dashboards contain: microburst timeline (per-region), per-route circuit hysteresis visualization, KV-cache hit vs microburst scatterplot, canary hourly report panel
Synthetic microburst canary runs in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 hourly for 48h without causing production degradation (canary must use isolated test tenant and rate-limited target routes)
Calibration job produces recommendations and stores a non-destructive suggested-params artifact in S3/Drive with diffable JSON per-route

E2E test: run chaos sim that kills 1 zone in region while generating microbursts in another region; system should failover according to policy and circuit hysteresis should prevent oscillation for at least 5 minutes
Runbook entries added to ops-docs with step-by-step guidance and rollback instructions
metrics_changes: Introduce request.microburst_flag (tagged by route, model, region, shard) — 1 when a microburst window exceeds microburst_window_ms threshold
Emit request.microburst_window_ms (rolling window used to detect burst in ms)
Emit request.microburst_count_in_1m (count of microburst events per route per 1m)
Augment request.token_latency_ms with token_index tag and sample_rate=1% default for full token streams (sampling increased to 10% for canary runs)
Add derived metric microburst.p95_delta_ms = p95(token_latency) - baseline.p50(token_latency) over burst windows
dashboard_panels: Microburst timeline: stacked area by region showing microburst_count_in_1m and overlay of request.qps
Per-route circuit state heatmap: rows=route, cols=minute buckets, color=circuit state (closed/half-open/open)
KV-cache hit vs microburst scatter: x=kv_cache_hit_rate, y=microburst.p95_delta_ms, points colored by model-family
Canary hourly summary: pass/fail, peak qps, peak token tail latency, synthetic-error-rate, recommended-params artifact link
Circuit hysteresis parameters table: open_threshold_ms, open_window_s, cooldown_s, backoff_multiplier, last_applied, last_recommended
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1879 — canary harness k8s job and k6 scenarios
test_plan: Unit tests for the microburst detector logic with synthetic traffic traces (edge cases: overlapping windows, burst merging)
Integration test: pipeline validates ingestion of new metrics and availability in metrics store
Canary test: run synthetic microburst generator against isolated test tenant in staging, validate calibration job output
Chaos sim: Gradual increase in microburst intensity while killing a zone to validate hysteresis prevents flapping
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased telemetry volume from token_index tagging may raise ingestion costs. Mitigation: default sample_rate=1% and raise only for canaries; add cardinality caps in ingestion pipeline.

Risk: Calibration recommendations could suggest aggressive shedding that impacts real customers. Mitigation: calibration outputs are non-destructive suggestions requiring manual review; add safety floor that never recommends shedding below X% of baseline capacity per route.
Risk: Canary runs could interfere with capacity. Mitigation: isolate canary to dedicated pool/tenant and use strict rate caps; require approval for production canaries.
notes_and_decisions: 2025-01-15: Decided to sample token streams by default at 1% to control cardinality; increase sampling during controlled canary runs.
2025-01-21: Agreed on metric names and tags in telemetry sync; storage team approved new derived metric microburst.p95_delta_ms.
2025-01-29: Chose k6 + a small Go harness for microburst generator to ensure precise inter-request timings (sub-10ms spacing).
2025-02-02: Opted to keep calibration proposals non-destructive for first rollout; follow-up ticket will implement auto-apply with safety checks.
